matrix.claim: Per-client case evidence for the exact tested head only; not a support window or release acceptance.

cases.description: Connect with the named ACL user and password, then PING.
The named user with +@all can SET and GET its own key.
The limited user receives NOPERM for SET outside its allowed commands.
RESP2 connection covers PING, SET/GET with binary bytes, INCR and HSET/HGETALL.
RESP3 (HELLO 3) connection covers the same roundtrip.
A batched pipeline returns ordered replies for every queued command.
MULTI/EXEC returns the ordered results and leaves committed state.
A subscriber receives a published binary payload from a second connection.
A command against the wrong type surfaces a WRONGTYPE client error.
An unknown command surfaces a client error without disconnecting.
A connection without credentials receives an authentication error.
A dropped connection reconnects and still reads the committed value.
TLS with the test CA authenticates and completes SET/GET.
TLS to a certificate without the target IP SAN is rejected.

resp3-roundtrip.detail_regex: ^resp3-hgetall-flat-array: the profile's bounded RESP3 subset returns arrays, not maps \(C6\)$
resp3-roundtrip.reason: The profile's RESP3 subset emits arrays rather than maps (C6), so redis-py surfaces HGETALL as a flat field/value array. The exact shape is asserted and frozen; if either side starts emitting maps, this case fails and the matrix must be reviewed.

resp3-roundtrip.reason: The profile's RESP3 subset emits arrays rather than maps (C6), so node-redis returns HGETALL as a flat field/value array under RESP3. The exact shape is asserted and frozen; a change on either side fails the matrix.
